idiom_name: interface + top-level when-factory (or companion factory) over a store key
implementation_notes: Kotlin keeps the DAO contract as an interface and replaces the factory hierarchy with a top-level function whose when-expression over a store enum returns the implementation, or with a companion object factory when the constructor needs parameters; interface delegation (class CachedUserDao(private val base: UserDao) : UserDao by base) makes DAO decoration free, which removes one common reason to build a class hierarchy. When the project has a DI container, it binds the store instead - Koin modules with named or qualified definitions, Hilt with @Provides factory methods - so the hand-written factory is a thin composition-root function, and the classic abstract factory is justified only in container-free or multiplatform code.
pitfalls: DAO classes needing constructor parameters cannot be bound with Hilt's @Binds directly; provide them through @Provides factory methods or the compiler error is opaque.
Suspending DAO methods force every implementation and wrapper to be suspend-aware; mixing blocking JDBC calls into a suspending DAO stalls the dispatcher thread.
Koin named/qualified definitions resolve at runtime, so a missing or misspelled definition throws at injection time - keep qualification constants in one place.
